item.title: This is now out of control, 7th August
item.description:
Greenwich Council should stop tolerating this. King William Walk has become Lime’s overflow warehouse, and now the plaza by Cutty Sark is following suit. Perhaps the council should hire a skip, invoice Lime for the removal costs, and return every bike to them in one go. Clearly the current approach isn’t working.

item.title: This is becoming really unfair, 7th August
item.description:
This is King William Walk today. A permit-holder-only residential road has effectively become a storage depot for Lime bikes. Residents pay for parking permits yet regularly find dozens of hire bikes occupying the available spaces. Today is particularly bad, with an excessive number of bikes lined up along the street. This isn’t an isolated incident—it’s become a recurring problem and is unfair to residents who rely on these spaces. Lime needs to remove the excess bikes and stop using this residential street as an overflow parking area.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): King William Walk, Greenwich

item.title: Vehicle has driven into my property and damaged the brickwork around my front door, 7th August
item.description:
A vehicle has driven into my property today and damaged the brickwork around my front door. I didn't see anything. My brother was the first person to notice the damage when he returned home. He left the property at around 5am and returned at approximately 12pm. So the incident is believed to have happened sometime between these times. I also spoke with my neighbour across the road to ask whether they saw or heard anything. They said that they heard a loud noise at around 10am but did not see what happened or the vehicle involved. I’m wondering if it might have happened when the bins were being collected this morning. Would you mind checking your camera, if you have one, to see if it captured anything? I’d really appreciate it. Thank you.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Beltwood Road, Lower Belvedere, Greater London

item.title: Summerfield Avenue, 7th August
item.description:
There are a number of overgrown and unmaintained front boundary hedges on the street (for many months) that are not only unsightly but also pose a safety hazard especially for young kids. Also, they take up a chunk of the pavement, restricting access to use the full pavement which is highly inconvenient especially for most of us with kids and prams. Hedges need to be trimmed back so they do not fall over the boundary wall and do not restrict free access to the pavement (which is public property).
